long_biography.plain_text:
Nightlife offered Paolo Pazzaglia a different kind of business from the former factories he later redeveloped in Bologna. He owned La Capannina on the city's hills and was associated with Peter Pan in Riccione. He said he entrusted those clubs to managers, judging that conversation over dinner had become more appealing than dancing.

His property work followed a more direct role. Giulia Srl, which he led, signed a planning agreement with Bologna for the former Officine Cevolani land. Pazzaglia then directed residential projects across adjoining disused sites, including P-Tower near the station and exhibition district. The developments replaced workshops and a foundry with housing while retaining the land within his business interests after industrial production moved away.

confidence.reason: Corriere's direct interview supports the club-operating approach and changing social preferences, while Bologna municipal documents and the city library establish planning and redevelopment. The descriptions of district transformation are bounded to reported projects.
